title: How digital cameras work
examples: How does the lens help the camera take a picture?
What is the difference between pixels and megapixels?
Does the image sensor capture the light or the color?

explain.say: The lens is the first part that collects the light.
The lens focuses all the light onto the image sensor.
The image sensor has millions of tiny dots called pixels.
Each pixel records a tiny bit of light and color information.
Megapixels tell you the total number of pixels on the sensor.
In real life, a digital camera uses these parts together. The lens gathers light, the sensor captures it as many pixels, and the megapixels count how many pixels there are.

faq.q: How much does the lens affect the picture?
faq.a: The lens controls how much and what kind of light reaches the sensor. A different lens can make the picture look zoomed in or wider.
asks: Does the lens change the picture?

faq.q: Are pixels responsible for the color?
faq.a: No, the pixels are the individual spots that record the light and color information. The sensor has millions of these spots working together.
asks: Where does the color come from?

faq.q: Why is megapixels a bigger number?
faq.a: Megapixels is just a way to count the total number of pixels available. More megapixels usually means you can print a bigger picture.
asks: Is megapixels the same as pixels?

faq.q: Does the sensor capture light or just color?
faq.a: The sensor captures the light that carries the color information. It records the intensity and the color spectrum of the light.

faq.q: If I use a zoom lens, what changes?
faq.a: Zooming changes how much of the scene fits onto the sensor. It makes things look closer or makes the view wider.
asks: Does the lens change the view?

facts: The lens gathers and focuses light onto the sensor.
The image sensor is made up of millions of tiny light-sensitive dots.
Each dot on the sensor is called a pixel.
Megapixels is the total count of these pixels.

quiz.say: If a camera has more megapixels, it can:

options.show: print a larger, more detailed image.
options.say: print a larger, more detailed image.

options.show: take a picture in low light.
options.say: take a picture in low light.

quiz.why: More pixels mean more data points, allowing for bigger prints.

wrong.0: Brightness is controlled by the aperture and shutter speed.
wrong.1: Zooming is controlled by the lens mechanism itself.
wrong.3: Low light is more about the sensor's sensitivity, not just the count.

quiz.say: What is the primary job of the lens?

options.show: to change the color of the light.
options.say: to change the color of the light.

options.show: to focus light onto the sensor.
options.say: to focus light onto the sensor.

quiz.why: The lens acts like a magnifying glass to gather light rays correctly.

wrong.0: The lens bends light; color changes are handled by filters or the sensor.
wrong.2: The memory card stores the data, not the lens.
wrong.3: The megapixels count the pixels, but the lens does not count.

quiz.say: If the sensor has many pixels, what does this mean?

options.show: the image can capture fine details.
options.say: the image can capture fine details.

quiz.why: More pixels mean more individual points to record details across the whole picture.

wrong.0: Brightness depends on the amount of light hitting the sensor.
wrong.1: Cost depends on many factors, not just pixel count.
wrong.2: Lens quality is separate from the sensor's pixel count.
